description: Private source contract only. No documentation endpoint, listener or SSO is enabled. Completed direct TLS 1.2+, exact configured Host/HTTPS Origin, canonical origin-form request, fresh Core Session and current exact-scope RBAC are mandatory. Read-only Deployment capability, approval catalog and management-scope requests require the cookie and explicit session channel; every mutation additionally requires the current CSRF proof. Authorization custody, encoded/alternate routing, Referer fallback, CORS and provider-token grants are forbidden. The reserved server is an example, never an operator default.

accountSessionCookie.name: __Host-mt_session
accountSessionCookie.description: One canonical nonzero Core mtas1 Account Session cookie. Fresh durable authentication, Deployment/recovery/generation and exclusive idle/absolute expiry checks apply. Never an IdP token, IaC credential or cached authority. Cookie issuance uses Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/ and no Domain.

sessionCSRF.name: X-MeshTransit-CSRF
sessionCSRF.description: One <=256-byte dedicated mtscsrf1 intent proof bound to the complete current Session bearer, exact Origin and Deployment. Require together with the cookie for mutations. Preparation lifetime is 30-120 whole seconds, shortened to exclusive Session expiry; no future issue time, expiry equality or skew grace. The proof is replayable intent transport, never an operation/Session grant.

ConsoleOrigin.name: Origin
ConsoleOrigin.description: One exact operator-configured HTTPS Origin, including canonical non-default port when configured. Missing/null/foreign Origin rejects; Referer, forwarded headers and normalization never replace it.

ConsoleSessionProof.description: Shape hint only. Core verifies the complete canonical envelope/MAC and exact cookie/Origin/Deployment/time binding before fresh durable Session authentication.

display_code.description: Immutable display label. UUID remains the canonical API and authorization identity.

can_rename.description: Presentation hint only. Rename rechecks live ownership.

permissions.description: Workspace-level permissions the Session holds, for presentation only; every action reauthorizes.

display_code.description: Immutable display label. UUID remains the canonical API and authorization identity.

ConsoleDeploymentCapabilities.description: Navigation evidence only. Profiles share one feature set; limits come from the verified Deployment entitlement (ADR-050). Without an entitlement a self-hosted Deployment reports the single-Workspace baseline.

network_revision.description: With include=status: the Network revision an in_sync Device holds; null when no row on the page receives policy (so nothing was read) or the revisions could not be read.

policy_revision.description: With include=status: the active policy revision; null as network_revision.

observations_available.description: With include=status: true when delivery records were read for the page's rows. false when they could not be read, and also when no row receives policy (network_revision is then null).

ownership.description: A member Device expires per profile and joins its owner's user groups; a Workspace Device never expires and survives staff changes.

owner.description: The owning member; null for a Workspace Device.

suspended_reason.description: admin: suspended by an administrator; handover: transferred to a member who has not yet signed in on the Device.

handover_to.description: The member a handover waits for.

dns_name.description: The Device's DNS name <label>.<workspace code>.<network code>.<suffix>, unique in the Network; null for a Device that holds no name (revoked or deleted) and for a Kubernetes gateway replica, which other Devices reach by its cluster's name (kubernetes_cluster.dns_name). The suffix is the deployment's (default mesh.internal).

advertised_prefixes.description: Subnets the Device offers to forward as a subnet router, from its own route settings: canonical CIDRs, IPv4 before IPv6, then by address and length. A list holds the first 16; one Device's read holds all. Offering grants nothing: an administrator still makes the Device a Site's router.

advertised_prefix_count.description: How many subnets the Device offers in all.

dns_name.description: The cluster's mesh DNS name <cluster>.kube.<workspace code>.<network code>.<suffix>: it resolves to the addresses of the replicas a Device may reach. null when the Network has no zone.

kubernetes_cluster.description: Present only on a Kubernetes gateway replica: its cluster. Access to a replica is granted to the whole cluster, never to the replica alone, so rules, DNS and shares name the cluster instead.

status.description: List only, with include=status; never on a single Device's read. null for a Device that receives no policy (expired, revoked, deleted) and when the Network revisions could not be read. When only delivery records could not be read the object is present with status and enforcement unknown and observations_available is false.

addresses.description: The mesh addresses peers reach the Device by, IPv4 before IPv6, without a prefix length; empty unless the Device is active or suspended and has not expired.

limited.description: The report holds only the Device's 256 busiest peers.

route_enforcement.description: Whether the router forwards into the served routes it was last delivered, compared by route digest v1, as enforcement compares the packet filter.

sites.description: The router's own health of each Site it serves; empty when it reported none in the last 30 seconds.

router.description: Present for a subnet router: its route enforcement and current Site health.

dns.description: Present for a Device that reports the DNS it applied (dns.root1, DNS design D1b §8).

enforcement.description: Whether the Device applies the DNS routes and search domains it was last delivered, compared by DNS digest v1, or why it applies none.

subnet_routes.description: The router the Device sends each Site's traffic through, as it last reported (within three minutes)

exit.description: The Exit Pool the Device sends its Internet traffic through and the exit node it uses, as it last reported (within three minutes).

via.description: sticky: kept although Core elected another exit node; none: no exit node can serve (exit_node_device_id is null).

name.description: The peer's hostname; null for a shared Device of another Network.

ConsoleDeviceListStatus.description: A row's connection and policy status, the same classification as the Device's own status read.

ConsoleDevicePlatform.description: What the Device's client says it runs on, from its latest session; null when unknown.

os.description: The operating system as Go names it: darwin, linux, windows, android, ios or freebsd.

ConsoleDevicePublicAddresses.description: The Device's addresses on the Internet from its latest endpoint report (what STUN saw, what its gateway mapped, public addresses of its interfaces), IPv4 first; empty when unknown. Readable under device.read.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the country the address is registered in (IP Geolocation by DB-IP); null when unknown or no country table is configured.

Unknown outcomes require a fresh read.

A window longer than 93 days is rejected as invalid_request; read older evidence window by window.

get.description: Requires guardrail.read on the Workspace. Guardrails are owner-level limits that no rule or share may break; they are checked when a rule is published and when a share is offered, accepted or enabled, and an enforce-mode guardrail also cuts the existing shares it blocks from maps.

can_manage.description: The reader holds guardrail.manage: create and narrow guardrails.

can_weaken.description: The reader holds guardrail.weaken: loosen, switch to audit or delete guardrails.

networks.description: Empty means every Network of the Workspace

post.description: Requires guardrail.manage. A guardrail only narrows what is reachable; at most 100 per Workspace. Every referenced Network must belong to the Workspace. An enforce-mode guardrail cuts the existing shares it blocks from maps, so it needs the impact_hash of a preview.

mode.description: audit records findings without blocking; enforce blocks

networks.description: Empty means every Network of the Workspace

post.summary: Preview what saving a guardrail does to existing shares
post.description: Requires guardrail.manage or guardrail.weaken. Reads the Workspace's active guardrails and active shares and returns the shares the guardrail would cut (enforce mode) or report (audit mode), with the impact_hash an enforce-mode create or update must send. Changes nothing. More than 20,000 active shares are refused with guardrail_impact_too_large; switching a guardrail to audit mode or deleting it needs no preview. While a guardrail of a Workspace is saved, offering, accepting or enabling a share of that Workspace answers a retryable conflict.

side.description: The Workspace's side of the share; both for a share between two of its Networks

network_id.description: The Workspace's own Network of the share (the provider's for both)

label.description: The access label the provider gave, or the consumer's Imported Resource name

patch.description: Replaces name, description, mode and parameters at the version in If-Match. Deleting, switching from enforce to audit, or letting through anything it used to block needs guardrail.weaken; adding or narrowing needs guardrail.manage. The kind never changes. A result in enforce mode needs the impact_hash of a preview; switching to audit mode or loosening restores the shares it no longer blocks. Above 20,000 active shares a result in enforce mode is refused with guardrail_impact_too_large, even when it loosens; switch the guardrail to audit mode or delete it instead. A share changed concurrently is retried by Core, then answered with version_conflict (412).

mode.description: audit records findings without blocking; enforce blocks

Deleting an enforced guardrail wakes the maps of at most 1,024 Networks at once; the others follow at the next map reconcile interval.

post.description: Requires member.manage and a delegation ceiling covering every role the member holds. Nobody removes the owner or themselves; a suspended member can be removed. Each Device the member owns in this Workspace is moved to the Workspace, handed to another active member of its Network (suspended until that member signs in on it), or revoked as the plan says; a Device the plan does not name is revoked. A Device waiting to be handed to the member stays suspended for an administrator. The member's enrollment keys here are revoked, they leave every Identity Group, their roles and Network memberships end, their Console sessions in this Workspace end, and the membership is revoked. An invitation can bring them back later.

post.description: Requires member.manage and a delegation ceiling covering every role the member holds. Nobody ends the sessions of the owner or themselves. Ends every active Console session the member signed in to this Workspace. Sessions the member signed in to other Workspaces, the membership, Devices and roles are unchanged; to cut the member off here, suspend them. The member must be active.

post.description: Requires member.manage and a delegation ceiling covering every role the member holds. Nobody suspends the owner or themselves. The IPv4 prefix must be /16–/28 inside 100.64.0.0/10 and the IPv6 prefix /56–/112; both must lie inside the Workspace overlay pools and must not overlap any other Network of the Workspace. Other Workspaces may reuse the same ranges. The creator gets a Network membership and an interactive enrollment profile. network_id is client-chosen for safe retries.

get.description: Requires device.read on the Network. Lists each tagged Device with its tag IDs; untagged Devices are omitted.

Fresh Session and exact device.read Role Binding are mandatory on every page. Devices come in byte order of (hostname, ID), removed ones included; q keeps names that start with it, state keeps Devices that can connect now (active) or cannot (inactive). The page token carries the search it continues. Registration state is not online presence or packet authority. No keys, credentials, endpoints or provider claims are disclosed.

post.description: Requires device.manage. Only a Device owned by a member, active or suspended, that does not already never expire and that expired or expires within a day can be extended. The new expiry is the duration from now and must be later than the old one; it lasts until the Device signs in again or is enrolled with a new key.
Requires device.quarantine. Resuming a Device that waits for handover cancels the handover; the owner is unchanged.
Requires device.quarantine. The Device keeps its identity, addresses, tags and groups but leaves every map at once. Answers the Device; ETag is its version.

Requires device.transfer. To the Workspace: takes effect at once, the Device stops expiring and leaves its former owner's user groups. To a member (an active member of the Workspace and Network): the Device is suspended until that member signs in on it, which completes the handover.

Members of the Network are always listed; the rest of the Workspace only when the caller can add them (network.member.manage) or read the Workspace's members (member.read). can_manage reports network.member.manage. A suspended Workspace member is listed but cannot be added.

post.description: Requires network.member.manage (the owner, admin, or an it_admin of the Workspace or of this Network). Adds up to 150 active Workspace members, each named once; a member already in the Network is reported unchanged. A member of the Network can enroll Devices into it and receive Devices handed over in it. A suspended Workspace member cannot be added. Maps are not rebuilt.

200.description: The memberships created and the members already in the Network

post.summary: Remove a member from a Network
post.description: Requires network.member.manage. Nobody removes the owner or themselves, and the actor must outrank each role the member holds in its own scope: a Workspace-scope role needs the owner or a Workspace-scope admin or it_admin who could grant it; a role bound to this Network may also be outranked by the actor's admin or it_admin role bound to this Network; a custom role binding of this Network needs a Workspace-scope assigner. Each Device the member owns in this Network is moved to the Workspace, handed to another active member of this Network (suspended until that member signs in on it), or revoked as the plan says; a Device the plan does not name is revoked. A Device of this Network waiting to be handed to the member stays suspended for an administrator. The enrollment keys they issued for this Network are revoked, their roles for this Network end, and the Network membership is revoked; a browser registration they started is refused at approval. Their Workspace membership, Identity Groups, other Networks and Console sessions are unchanged.

new_owner_id.description: Required for transfer_member and absent otherwise

200.description: The removed membership and what happened to each of the member's Devices in the Network

get.summary: Resolve a share's consumer Network by its 12-digit display code
get.description: Lets a caller holding share.offer on the provider Network address a Network in any Workspace of the same Deployment by display code. Only existence is revealed: public IDs and display codes, never names. cross_workspace reports a target outside the provider Workspace; such a share is accepted separately in the consumer Workspace.

200.description: An active Network in this Deployment

403.description: permission_denied: no share.offer on the provider Network

404.description: share_target_not_found: no active Network has this display code

post.summary: Grant one built-in role to a Workspace member
post.description: Owners may grant every role; admin and it_admin may grant only the roles below them. Nobody changes their own roles and the owner holds no assignments. assignment_id is client-chosen: retrying the same request returns 200 with the original assignment, while reusing it for another request conflicts. Unknown outcomes require a fresh member read.

post.summary: Durably revoke the current Core Session
post.description: Require the current host-only Session cookie and a fresh proof bound to that exact cookie, Origin and Deployment. Atomically revoke only the matching active Session in the current recovery epoch, then expire only __Host-mt_session. Concurrent or completed revocation is an idempotent no-match. No provider token, upstream logout, alternate cookie, redirect or authority renewal is performed. JSON whitespace around the literal empty object is allowed.

204.description: The current Core Session is durably ended and its browser cookie is expired. The response has no body.

Set-Cookie.description: Exact host-only deletion for the Core Session cookie; no Domain or other cookie is changed.

schema.const: __Host-mt_session=; Path=/; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:01 GMT; Max-Age=0; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax

default.description: Private pre-release failure leaves status/headers/body untouched. Authentication failures use the existing bounded management denial without clearing or renewing cookies. Durable submission failure is uncertain delivery, never non-commit evidence or an automatic retry.

post.summary: End every Core Session of the signed-in Account
post.description: Require the current host-only Session cookie and a fresh proof bound to that exact cookie, Origin and Deployment. Atomically advance the Account's session generation and end every active Core Session of the Account in every Workspace, including the current one, then expire only __Host-mt_session. Devices are not affected. A Session that another sign-out already ended gets the bounded authentication denial and ends nothing. No provider token, upstream logout, alternate cookie, redirect or authority renewal is performed. JSON whitespace around the literal empty object is allowed.

204.description: Every Core Session of the Account is durably ended and the browser cookie is expired. The response has no body.

Set-Cookie.description: Exact host-only deletion for the Core Session cookie; no Domain or other cookie is changed.

schema.const: __Host-mt_session=; Path=/; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:01 GMT; Max-Age=0; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax

default.description: Private pre-release failure leaves status/headers/body untouched. Authentication failures use the existing bounded management denial without clearing or renewing cookies. Durable submission failure is uncertain delivery, never non-commit evidence or an automatic retry.

get.summary: List current Session management scopes for Console navigation
get.description: Return only the login Workspace and a UUIDv7-keyset page of active Networks with current explicitly bound inventory, policy or sharing permissions. Navigation is not authorization. Every inventory read and management action rechecks its exact permission and scope. No CSRF proof, request body, Authorization credential, Session identifier or provider claim is accepted or returned.

200.description: Fresh server-authoritative management-scope projection for the current Session login Workspace.

default.description: Bounded generic authentication, request, rate-limit or availability failure. No Session, membership, role-binding or cross-scope evidence is disclosed.

post.summary: Prepare current-Session intent without issuing or renewing authority
post.description: Consume shared source/Session budgets and freshly authenticate the existing cookie before independent OS entropy. Return only the proof and exclusive expiry. No Set-Cookie, provider token, identity or resource grant. JSON whitespace around the literal empty object is allowed. Existing private transport/body/header/cookie/capacity/deadline bounds and zero-output pre-release failure apply.

200.description: No-grant proof for the current Session. Cookie is never set, renewed or cleared.

default.description: Private pre-release failure leaves status/headers/body untouched. No public HTTP error mapper is enabled. Submission failure is uncertain delivery, never non-commit evidence, retry or response rewrite.

post.summary: Move the current Session to another Workspace
post.description: Rebind the current Session to a Workspace from listSessionWorkspaces without signing in again. The Session version increments, so requests still bound to the previous Workspace fail their exact-version check and the Console reloads its scope. Switching to the current Workspace returns replayed true and changes nothing. A committed switch appends one audit record.

503.description: Temporarily unavailable or uncertain; refresh before retrying

get.summary: List the Workspaces the current Session may switch to
get.description: Return at most 100 Workspaces where the signed-in Account holds an active membership, the Workspace is active, and it routes the Session's identity provider and client: the same rules as browser login. current marks the Workspace bound to the Session. Listing grants nothing; every management action rechecks its own permission.

get.summary: Read the current server-authoritative Deployment capability projection

The projection is for Console navigation and route guards only. It grants no Workspace, platform, billing or operation authority; unknown, cloud, contradictory or stale authority fails closed.

200.description: Fresh non-secret Deployment capability projection for the authenticated Console Session.

default.description: Bounded generic authentication, request, rate-limit, unsupported-profile or availability failure. No entitlement, installation key, Session or topology evidence is disclosed.

post.summary: Change many DNS names at once
post.description: Requires dns.manage on the Network and MESHTRANSIT_DNS_ZONES_ENABLED (dns_zones_disabled otherwise). Up to 100 operations, each on its own name, in one transaction: the checks see the zone as the request leaves it, so a name can be deleted and created again as another kind. A failing operation fails all; error.operation_index names it (from 0). One rate-limit token, one revision, one audit event per changed name.
